hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there something good in your life right now that you’d hate to take for granted?
options: then keep them in mind. this story is about exactly that.
most of us do sometimes. listen to this one.
that’s honest. the story might help you spot one.

steps.line: The Qur’an tells of a man with two gardens, heavy with grapes, ringed with date palms, a stream running between them.
He walked through them with a friend and said, “I don’t think this will ever end.”

steps.q: His friend has a question for him. What do you think he asks?
o: “Did you thank the workers who built this?”
“Why didn’t you name God when you came in?”
“Have you shared any of it with the poor?”
steps.why: He asked why the man hadn’t named where the garden came from. Watch which words he meant.

steps.line: His friend asked: when you came into your garden, why didn’t you say, “Ma sha’ Allah,” what God has willed? There is no strength except in God.

steps.q: Why would the friend want him to say “what God has willed” about his own garden?
o: To admit the garden was a gift, not only his doing
To make the garden grow faster
Because the garden really belonged to the friend
steps.why: Mashallah says: this good thing is a gift. The man thought it was all his, and that it would last forever.

steps.line: Then the harvest was struck down. The vines fell onto their trellises, and the man wrung his hands over everything he had spent.
In the same chapter, the Qur’an says: never say of anything, “I will do it tomorrow,” without adding, “if God wills.” In sha’ Allah.

steps.q: Many commentators say this verse came after the Prophet ﷺ told people, “I’ll answer you tomorrow,” without adding “if God wills.” What happened?
o: The answer came the next morning
The answer didn’t come for days
steps.why: In the well-known account, revelation paused for days, and the answer came with this verse. Even the Prophet ﷺ was taught to say it.

steps.line: So today: inshallah, if God wills, for plans still ahead. Mashallah, what God has willed, for good that’s already here.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Your friend shows you her newborn, and a Muslim friend beside you says “mashallah.” What is that word guarding against, many believe?
o: Seeming to boast for the parents
Praise that could turn into envy
Tempting fate by naming the future
steps.why: Many Muslims say mashallah when admiring a baby or a new home, so the praise points to God and not to envy. A saying of the Prophet ﷺ calls the evil eye real.

say: here’s what i love. the friend didn’t tell him to stop enjoying his garden. he told him to name where it came from.
in islam, that’s the difference. inshallah: make your plan, and hold tomorrow with an open hand. mashallah: see the good that’s here, and call it a gift.

steps.q: Saying inshallah doesn’t mean you stop planning. What does the Qur’an’s line really ask?
o: Plan only what you can control
Make real plans, and hold them humbly
steps.why: The verse doesn’t forbid “tomorrow.” It asks you to add “if God wills”: plan for real, and stay honest that the future isn’t yours to promise.

today.say: today, when you talk about a plan, add “if God wills,” even quietly. and when you see something good, say “mashallah,” or just name it as a gift.
options: lovely. one for tomorrow, one for today.
that’s a beautiful place to start. good things look different when you name them.

tomorrow.title: Is doubt okay?
tomorrow.line: a prophet looks up at the stars, and keeps asking.
